handoff: review#1: D1–D5 code sound and tested at S1. Blocking in skill texts: subagent brief uses 'norn story wait --until parked' (not a valid condition; F1); norn-fsd loads norn-fsd-round via the Skill tool but it has disable-model-invocation: true (F2). Minor: run view mark untested, story edit --reason dropped before start, view re-reads all rounds' receipts per load. Traceability table in handoff.

findings.title: Subagent brief waits with `--until parked`, which is not a wait condition
findings.detail:
The brief says `norn story wait <story> --until parked`. `story wait` accepts only step=<name>, gate, ask, stuck, done, merged (packages/view/src/wait.ts:15). A parked value is a usage error ('bad --until'), so every subagent fails on its first wait. A subagent also needs to wake on gate, ask, stuck and the round's end, but --until takes one condition. The docs command lint (test/repo/docs.test.ts) checks flags, not their values, so nothing caught this. Spec B5: "each looping on `norn story wait <story> --until …` in the foreground".
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Use a condition that exists and covers every reason to wake (e.g. accept several conditions in `--until gate,ask,stuck,done`, or have the brief wait with a bounded --timeout and read `story view --json`). Add an assets test or lint that checks each `--until` value printed in a bundled skill parses with parseWaitCondition.

findings.title: norn-fsd tells the agent to load norn-fsd-round, which is set so the model cannot load it
findings.detail:
norn-fsd says "Load the `norn-fsd-round` skill and follow all of it". norn-fsd-round's frontmatter has `disable-model-invocation: true`, so in Claude Code the Skill tool refuses to load it. The person starts only norn-fsd, so its agent cannot get the protocol it depends on. The subagent brief says "act … by the rules of norn-fsd-round", which the subagents cannot load either. Plan D6: "norn-fsd-round holds the whole protocol; norn-fsd links to it … so every subagent gets the same rules."
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Either drop disable-model-invocation from norn-fsd-round (B2 is still enforced by the .norn-unit stop and the delegated_in_unit refusal), or have norn-fsd and the brief name the file to read (the linked skill's SKILL.md path) instead of loading a skill. Pin the choice in the assets test.

findings.title: B21 names `norn run view`; only `run list` is asserted
findings.detail:
B21's example: "`norn run view gh-201` shows 'approve-slices: approve — delegated (supervisor): …'". The test asserts the mark in `run list --json` and in the `run list` markdown. The receiptSummary marks (timeline.ts) used by the trace timeline and run view have no assertion.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add one assertion on `norn run view gh-1 --json` (or its markdown) for the delegated mark.

findings.title: `--reason` without `--delegated` on a not-yet-started workflow edit is accepted and dropped
findings.detail:
With --workflow on an unstarted story (or a slice switch), `--reason "…"` passes validation, but delegatedFields(d) is used only in the round branch, so the reason goes nowhere without a word. The option help says it applies to a started story only.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Refuse `--reason` as a usage error when the edit is not a round start, like `--delegated` already is.

findings.title: The project view re-reads and validates every round's receipts for every story on each load
findings.detail:
delegatedDecisions calls storyRounds + listReceipts for each story in loadProjectView, which `status --segment` (run by Herdr every few seconds, HC13) and the cockpit call. Earlier-round receipts are immutable, so this repeats the same IO on every refresh, and it grows with history.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Read earlier rounds only for story view/orient, or cache by round folder; keep status's count cheap.

findings.title: The watch check does not name the field it reads
findings.detail:
`norn status --json` has no heartbeat field; a stale watch shows as an unblock item with id `heartbeat:…`. The skill says only 'No heartbeat', so the agent has to guess what to look for.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Name the unblock item (`groups.unblock[].id` starting `heartbeat:`).
